slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Many squamous epithelial cells mean saliva contamination: more than 25 per low-power (×100) field — a poor specimen; the best specimens have fewer than 10 squamous cells and more than 25 leukocytes per field. Interpret with care or ask for a repeat specimen.
A watery specimen, or one mixed with food or nasal mucus, is unsuitable.
Drugs (for example rifampicin) can change the colour of sputum.

A good specimen is essential for a reliable analysis; Aripova advises keeping in the laboratory a set of unstained smears made from positive sputum and checking each new batch of stain alongside every specimen.

slides.title: Sources of error, reading and quality control
bullets: If the dye boils or overheats, or the slide is left dry, the staining is spoiled; leftover water interferes with the next dye.
If the smear is not fully decolourised, traces of carbol-fuchsin spoil the result.
How to read a Ziehl–Neelsen smear (colour, grading and counting) is not given in the source — use the laboratory’s approved instructions.
Internal quality control: keep a set of unstained smears made from positive sputum; check a new batch of dye or another reagent on a control smear stained together with every specimen.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: The colour is light-sensitive: keep the working reagent protected from light and do not use it past its date.
Standard and sample must be treated under the same conditions (temperature, incubation time); volumes are measured with sound pipettes.
A haemolysed, turbid or lipaemic sample may distort the result — take a new one.
If the result is above the limit of linearity, dilute the sample and repeat.
Quality control: measure the control material in every analytical series and record the result on the control chart.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Deviations in temperature (37 °C) and incubation time directly affect the kinetic measurement.
If the working reagent is out of date or was stored wrongly (outside 2–8 °C), NADH breaks down and the result is distorted.
Do not test haemolysed, turbid or lipaemic samples.
The manual says ALT can also be determined with a calibrator of known enzyme activity, and that accuracy must be checked with control sera.
Quality control: measure a control serum in every analytical series and record the result on the control chart.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: If the working reagent is out of date or wrongly stored, NADH breaks down and the measurement is wrong.
The timing of the A1 and A2 readings (30 and 60 seconds) must be kept exactly.
A haemolysed or turbid sample may distort the result.
If the result is above the limit of linearity, dilute the sample and repeat.
Quality control: measure a control serum in every analytical series and record the result on the control chart.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Keep the incubation times exactly (10 minutes for total, exactly 5 minutes for conjugated).
Observe the shelf life of the working reagent (5 days at 2–8 °C in the dark) and the colour stability of 1 hour in the dark.
A haemolysed sample is unsuitable — take non-haemolysed serum.

slides.title: Sources of error and quality control
bullets: Match the sample with the request form; if the result contradicts the clinical picture, check it again.
Quality control: measure a control serum in every analytical series and record the result on the control chart.
